title: Map Gmail metadata representation and excluded content

findings.invariant: Unsupported attachment bodies and the MIME depth-8 projection limit should be reported on the persisted event when attachments are present.
findings.observed: coverage.add('attachment_body_unsupported') always runs for filename or attachmentId parts, and coverage starts with mime_projection_limited_depth_8, but metadata.body_coverage is replaced with ['body_not_selected'] unless selected includes text. Attachment-only mapping keeps metadata.attachments_downloaded=false and omits the walk tokens.
findings.independently_expected: packages/connector-gmail/README.md states attachment bodies are unsupported and MIME inspection reports the projection limit.
findings.required_fix: Not in R055 write scope. P051/P052 must not assume attachment_body_unsupported survives attachments-only capture. A later owned change could persist walk coverage independently of the text field.

findings.invariant: Thread identifiers that survive live mapping should be named honestly on deletion observations.
findings.observed: Live events always set metadata.thread_id from Message.threadId. Tombstones persist message_id and history_id only.
findings.required_fix: Documented limitation for downstream; source_record_id still identifies account+message id.

findings.observed: Only depth-0 from, to, cc, subject, date, content-type persist under metadata.headers. Message-ID, Reply-To, In-Reply-To, References, MIME-Version, X-* and nested part headers are dropped. Last duplicate wins. Unselected headers omit the key.
findings.independently_expected: docs/gmail.md: header/label selections persist within metadata; not a claim of full RFC 2822 header capture.
